title: Long Multiplication and Division (KS2)
subject: Maths
strapline: Written methods for multiplying and dividing bigger numbers.
facts: Long multiplication multiplies by each digit in turn, keeping columns lined up.
When you multiply by the tens digit, put a 0 in the ones column first (it stands for ×10).
Then add your rows together to get the final answer.
Short division (the "bus stop" method) divides digit by digit from the left, carrying remainders across.
A remainder is what is left over when a number does not divide exactly.
You can estimate first (round the numbers) to check your answer is sensible.
Long division works the same way but you write out the subtraction at each step.

quick_quiz.q: When multiplying by the tens digit, what do you write in the ones column first?
What is the name for what is left over in a division?

teacher_tips: Insist on lined-up columns — most errors are place-value slips, not table errors.
Estimate before and check after, every time.
Link the "0 for the tens row" to place value so it isn't a magic rule.
